name: Lavender
grown_as: English lavender, an evergreen shrub. Drawn as a typical violet-purple English lavender such as 'Munstead' or 'Hidcote'. The library also lists Lavandula × allardii 'Meerlo', which looks quite different: a tall plant with broader, toothed, cream-edged leaves and long pale spikes. ⚠️ CHECK which lavender William grows, and whether 'Meerlo' needs its own drawing.
habit: A rounded, dome-shaped evergreen shrub 40 to 80 cm high and as wide, woody at the base, with many upright, leafless flower stalks rising above the leafy mound in summer.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, crowded on the shoots, with small tufts of leaves in the joints
leaf.outline: Long and very narrow, 2 to 5 cm long and 2 to 5 mm wide
leaf.surface: Covered in fine grey felt, whiter on young shoots

flower.petals: Joined; a larger two-lobed upper lip and a three-lobed lower lip
flower.behind: A hairy, ribbed, tube-shaped calyx, grey-purple, which carries much of the colour and stays after the flower falls; small brown papery bracts under each ring
flower.carried: In rings of 6 to 10 packed into a slender spike 2 to 8 cm long at the top of a long, bare, square, unbranched stalk 10 to 30 cm long, held well above the leaves; the lowest ring often a little apart
flower.size: Flowers about 1 cm long; spikes about 1 cm thick

fruit: Small brown nutlets inside the dry calyces; the spikes fade to grey-brown.
winter: Evergreen: a grey mound of leafy shoots, the old flower stalks cut off or left grey and dry.

leaf: a long very narrow leaf with a blunt tip
bloom: a slender spike of rings of small violet-purple flowers
the spike on top of a long bare stalk
young: a small grey-green bushy mound of narrow leaves in pairs
flower: many long bare stalks rising well above a grey mound
each ending in a slender violet-purple spike

look_alikes: Lavandin (Lavandula × intermedia) is bigger, with longer, often branched stalks and longer, paler, pointed spikes. French lavender (Lavandula stoechas) has short fat heads topped by purple 'ears'. Rosemary has dark green leaves white beneath and flowers in the leaf joints. Hyssop has green leaves and blue spikes among the leaves.
